mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the rate increase signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the unemployment rate increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the periods following the consumption increase.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates supply chain disruptions or a slowdown in manufacturing, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the industrial production drop.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with low interest rates
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the inflation and low-rate signal.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the labor market improvement signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the periods following the increase in housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% in a month and real GDP (GDPC1) shows a quarter-over-quarter increase, it signals a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% in 1 month and GDPC1 shows QoQ increase
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the economic expansion signal.
